steps.say: Vertigo is the illusion of movement, and the first split is peripheral with central disease. Peripheral vertigo is violent with deafness with vomiting but spares the brainstem, while central vertigo is mild with slurred speech with ataxia. Direction fixed nystagmus with hearing loss points outward, while direction changing nystagmus with normal hearing points inward. This split decides scan versus couch treatment.
steps.tx: **Vertigo** is illusory movement; the first split is **peripheral** versus **central**. Peripheral vertigo is violent with **deafness and vomiting** but no brainstem signs. Central vertigo is milder with **dysarthria and ataxia**. **Unidirectional nystagmus** with hearing loss points peripheral; **bidirectional** nystagmus points central.

steps.say: Benign positional vertigo strikes for seconds when rolling in bed, because loose crystals slide in the posterior canal. The Dix Hallpike test drops the head back and reproduces upbeating nystagmus after a few seconds of delay. The Epley manoeuvre rolls the crystals home and cures most cases in one sitting. No scan with no drugs is needed when the story with the test is classic.
steps.tx: **BPPV** gives seconds of spinning on **rolling in bed**; loose debris floats in the posterior canal. **Dix Hallpike** reproduces upbeating nystagmus after seconds of latency. The **Epley manoeuvre** rolls debris home and cures most in one sitting. Classic story plus classic test needs **no scan and no drugs**.

steps.say: Vestibular neuritis follows a virus and burns one labyrinth, leaving days of spinning with vomiting without a single brainstem sign. Hearing is completely spared, which separates it from labyrinthitis where the cochlea is hit too. The head impulse test fails toward the dead side, and steroids speed recovery. Most patients are steady within weeks as the brain compensates.
steps.tx: **Vestibular neuritis** follows viral illness: days of spinning with vomiting, **hearing spared**, no brainstem signs. **Labyrinthitis** adds hearing loss to the same picture. **Head impulse** fails toward the dead side. **Steroids** speed recovery; vestibular exercises complete it, and most patients are steady within weeks as the brain compensates.

points: Hearing spared, one labyrinth dead, recovers well
left.title: Vestibular neuritis

points: Hearing lost too, cochlea hit, protect hearing
right.title: Labyrinthitis

steps.say: Meniere disease swells the inner ear with fluid and attacks in a triad of spinning with roaring tinnitus with a blocked full ear. Hearing falls with each attack and never fully returns, so audiometry worsens year by year. Low salt with diuretic therapy spaces the attacks, and destructive gentamicin with surgery is reserved for deaf ears that still spin. Bilateral disease forbids destruction.
steps.tx: **Meniere disease** attacks with **vertigo, tinnitus and aural fullness**; hearing falls stepwise. **Low salt** with diuretic therapy spaces attacks. **Intratympanic gentamicin** with surgery is reserved for non-serviceable ears. **Bilateral** disease is never destroyed. Migraine with transient ischaemia mimics it, so vascular risks are always reviewed.

steps.say: Vestibular migraine spins without headache half the time, which is why it is missed. Attacks run minutes to hours with light sensitivity and a family history of headache. Motion sickness from childhood with a normal ear examination supports it. Migraine prevention with trigger control spaces attacks, while triptans abort severe ones. The ears are normal, so treatment follows the head, not the labyrinth.
steps.tx: **Vestibular migraine** spins for minutes to hours, often **without headache**; photophobia with family history gives it away. **Childhood motion sickness** with normal ears supports it. **Migraine prevention** with trigger control spaces attacks. **Triptans** abort severe spells. Normal hearing separates it from Meniere.

steps.say: The H I N T S examination is better than early M R I for stroke in acute vestibular syndrome. A normal head impulse with direction changing nystagmus with skew deviation means the brainstem, not the ear. Any one central sign triggers stroke protocol with thrombolysis considered. Peripheral patterns are reassuring, but vascular risks still earn observation. All three components are documented every time.
steps.tx: **HINTS** beats early MRI in acute vestibular syndrome: **normal head impulse**, direction changing nystagmus and **skew deviation** mean stroke. Any central sign triggers **stroke protocol**. **Peripheral HINTS** (failed impulse, one way nystagmus, no skew) reassures. **Vascular risks** still earn a period of observation.

steps.say: A vestibular schwannoma grows on the balance nerve and deafens one ear slowly over years. Tinnitus with imbalance with numbness of the face follows as the tumour fills the corner between pons with cerebellum. Gadolinium M R I of the internal auditory meatus finds lesions of millimetres, and small tumours are watched yearly. Surgery with focused radiation is reserved for growing or large tumours with brainstem pressure.
steps.tx: **Vestibular schwannoma** deafens **one ear slowly** over years with tinnitus and imbalance; facial numbness follows. **Gadolinium MRI** of the meatus finds millimetre lesions. **Small tumours** are watched yearly. **Surgery or focused radiation** is reserved for growing lesions and brainstem pressure.

steps.say: Bilateral loss of balance with bouncing vision on walking means both labyrinths have failed, usually after aminoglycoside treatment. Oscillopsia on head movement with a failed head impulse on both sides confirms it, and no drug restores dead hair cells. Stopping the toxin early with balance retraining is the whole treatment. Drug charts are reviewed in every new bilateral case.
steps.tx: **Bilateral vestibulopathy** gives **oscillopsia** (bouncing vision) on walking after **aminoglycoside** treatment. **Head impulse fails both sides**. No drug restores dead hair cells; **stop the toxin** and retrain balance. **Drug charts** are reviewed in every bilateral case, and **genetic testing** follows idiopathic ones.

steps.say: Treatment follows the named cause and little else is needed. Positional vertigo is repositioned on the couch, while neuritis receives steroids with exercises. Meniere starts with salt restriction with diuretic therapy and ends with ablation only for useless ears. Migraine is prevented as migraine, and schwannoma is watched until growth forces action. Symptom suppressants are kept to days, because they slow compensation.
steps.tx: **Cause decides treatment:** BPPV is **repositioned**, neuritis gets **steroids** with exercises, Meniere starts with **salt restriction** and diuretic therapy, migraine gets **prevention**, schwannoma is **watched** till growth. **Suppressants** (prochlorperazine, cinnarizine) run for **days only**, as they slow compensation and delay the brain learning again.

steps.say: The deadly trap is calling a cerebellar stroke positional vertigo, which kills when the patient is sent home. Vomiting with hiccups with crossed signs with severe ataxia is Wallenberg syndrome until scanned. Sudden deafness with vertigo is a labyrinthine emergency needing steroids within days. And every recurrent positional case is retested, because canals switch and the manoeuvre must switch too.
steps.tx: **Exam traps:** cerebellar **stroke** mimics peripheral vertigo; ataxia with dysarthria means scan. **Wallenberg** gives crossed signs with hiccups. **Sudden deafness** with vertigo needs steroids within days. **HINTS central** beats MRI early. **Recurrent BPPV** changes canals; retest before repeating Epley, and teach Brandt Daroff exercises for home use.

steps.say: For the exam, the facts to lock in are seconds on rolling for B P P V with Epley cure, H I N T S central for stroke, triad with stepwise deafness for Meniere, hearing spared for neuritis, and one sided years long deafness for schwannoma. Suppressants run days only and ablation never touches bilateral disease. Memorise the facts in this table exactly as written.
steps.tx: **High yield for the exam:** seconds on **rolling** mark BPPV; **Epley** cures. **HINTS central** marks stroke. **Triad with stepwise deafness** marks Meniere. **Hearing spared** marks neuritis. **Years long one sided deafness** marks schwannoma. Suppressants run **days only**, since longer use slows brain compensation.
